questions.stem: What does attribute-based access control (ABAC) in Unity Catalog base its policies on?

options.text: Governed tags on catalogs, schemas, tables and columns

questions.explanation: Attributes are governed tags, which can be set on catalogs, schemas, tables and columns, so one policy can cover many objects.

questions.stem: Why use an ABAC policy rather than setting a mask on each table by hand?

options.text: One policy applies to every table with a matching tag, including new ones

questions.explanation: A policy takes effect on any object with the attributes it targets, like a future grant, so rules scale as tables are added.

questions.stem: Which can an ABAC policy apply to matching tables? Choose two.
questions.explanation: ABAC policies apply row filters and column masks based on tags.

questions.stem: At which levels can an ABAC policy be defined so that it covers objects below it?
questions.explanation: A policy set on a catalog or schema applies to matching objects inside it.

questions.stem: Arrange the steps to protect phone numbers across many tables with ABAC.

options.text: Check the policy with SHOW EFFECTIVE POLICIES or DESCRIBE POLICY
Create a policy that applies the mask to columns with that tag
Tag the phone columns with a governed tag

questions.explanation: In this workflow the function and the tags exist before the policy, which you then check. The function and the tags can come in either order.
